turns: Should the published ETR be revised?
items.question: Why?
items.text:
Answer from platform data. The AI is not available right now.
[DC-D4-ETR-GLOBAL] DC-D4-ETR-GLOBAL: decided on time.
prior_answers:
The evidence does not show a revision is due, because it holds nothing newer than the published estimate to compare against. The published global ETR was issued at Sep 28, 13:30 ET, with a median restoration estimate of 79.4 h. DOM 14.206 calls for a revision when the median moves beyond its set margin; smaller moves are logged, not released. [1] You would propose a revision on F-DOM-121, and it needs the Incident Commander and the Duty Manager to sign. [2][3]

Sources:
[1] DOM 14.206 Rev K, Revision Summary; 1.0 PURPOSE; 6.0 PROCEDURE, pp. 1-3: "6.4.2 Revise a published ETR when the P50 moves by more than 12 h.6.4.3 A move of 12 h or less is logged but not released."
[2] DOM 14.206 Rev K, Revision Summary; 1.0 PURPOSE; 6.0 PROCEDURE, pp. 1-3: "6.2.3 The ETR Specialist proposes the global ETR on F-DOM-121 with the model inputs attached."
[3] DOM 14.206 Rev K, Revision Summary; 1.0 PURPOSE; 6.0 PROCEDURE, pp. 1-3: "6.4.4 Revised ETRs need the same approvals as in 6.2.4."

items.question: Where can I check which deadlines were met or missed?
items.text: The After-action page is the place for this. Its Deadlines tab shows which decisions were approved by their decide-by time (met) and which were approved late or never (missed). The same page also covers emergency approvals, ETR accuracy, the timeline and the regulator report. If you want to see a single decision and what became of it, the Decisions page opens each one on its own page, and the buttons below open both pages.
